page: Microsoft Azure D64ns_v6 is a network-optimized, general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dnv6 server family. Powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It lacks local storage and integrated GPU hardware, but supports premium external storage configurations.

The underlying x86_64 architecture includes advanced instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which accelerate vector and matrix operations. The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1 data cache per core. Cryptographic operations are accelerated via hardware-level AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instructions.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance in several key areas. The instance achieved a PassMark CPU score of 67,051.45, with strong results in extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 347.46 GB/sec, and static web serving throughput peaked in the top tier at 90.06 GB/sec. Redis SET operations performed strongly at 71.06 million operations per second. However, memory performance presents a notable tradeoff; while cached small-block read bandwidth is strong at 4,125.39 GB/sec, the PassMark memory score is categorized as weak at 1,568.49. Large-block uncached read and write bandwidths remain average at 148.18 GB/sec and 70.19 GB/sec, respectively.

Given its high-frequency dedicated cores and network optimization, the D64ns_v6 is well-suited for high-throughput static web serving, database operations, and multi-threaded decompression tasks. It also demonstrates strong capabilities for CPU-based LLM inference, particularly for prompt processing. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the lack of bundled local storage and GPUs positions this instance as a resource-dense option for compute-heavy and network-bound workloads that rely on external premium storage, avoiding the overhead of unused local disk resources.
